title: How to determine if a company is a good fit for you? ｜ 如何判断一家公司是否适合你？

sents.en: On paper, the job seemed perfect for me: The position was completely in line with my degree, the duties and responsibilities were compatible with my interests, and the office maintained a well-stocked kitchen that would satisfy my every snack desire.
sents.cn: 从纸面上看，这份工作对我来说堪称完美：职位与我的专业完全对口，职责与我兴趣相投，办公室还备有充足的零食，能满足我对零食的一切渴望。

sents.en: Sounds like my dream job, right?
sents.cn: 听起来像是我的理想工作，对吧？

sents.en: There was only one small problem: I simply didn't get along with the company culture.
sents.cn: 只有一个小问题：我实在无法适应这家公司的文化。

sents.en: They favored a more rigid, closed-door, corporate atmosphere, while I would have preferred something more collaborative and open.
sents.cn: 他们偏好更刻板、封闭的企业氛围，而我更想要协作、开放的氛围。

sents.en: They were complete clock watchers, while I would have liked a more flexible schedule.
sents.cn: 他们完全是盯着打卡的人，而我更希望有灵活的时间表。

sents.en: To put it plainly, we just weren't on the same page.
sents.cn: 直说吧，我们根本不是一路人。

sents.en: When it comes to looking for a new job, you already know that a big part of the interview process involves the company evaluating whether or not you're a good fit for their open role.
sents.cn: 说到找新工作，你已经知道面试流程的很大一部分是公司评估你是否符合其空缺职位。

sents.en: But, it's important to keep in mind that the employer isn't the only one who needs to identify a good match·you should be looking for that same exact thing.
sents.cn: 但重要的是谨记，需要识别良好匹配的并非只有雇主——你也应寻找同样的东西。

sents.en: Company culture can have a big impact on how you feel about your work, so you want to make sure you sign an offer letter with an organization you're truly excited about.
sents.cn: 企业文化会极大影响你对自己工作的感受，所以你要确保与一家自己真正向往的组织签下录用通知。

sents.en: However, figuring out what a company is like before you actually work there can be a bit of a challenge.
sents.cn: 然而，在实际入职前弄清一家公司究竟如何，可能有点挑战。

sents.en: Luckily, there are a few things you can do to determine whether or not a company is a good fit for you·before you ever sign your name on that dotted line.
sents.cn: 幸运的是，在你在虚线上签下名字之前，有几件事你可以做，来判断一家公司是否适合你。

sents.en: First of all, know what you want.
sents.cn: 首先，明确自己想要什么。

sents.en: It's hard to make any decisions when you don't really know what you're looking for.
sents.cn: 当你并不真正知道自己寻求什么时，很难做出任何决定。

sents.en: So before you can determine whether you and a specific company would be compatible together, it's important to have a solid handle on what exactly you want from your employer.
sents.cn: 所以在判断你与某家公司是否合拍之前，重要的是切实弄清你究竟希望从雇主那里得到什么。

sents.en: Many of us have an easier time identifying the things that we absolutely don't want.
sents.cn: 我们许多人都更容易找出自己绝对不想要的东西。

sents.en: If those are the only things you can think of, don't worry!
sents.cn: 如果那只是你能想到的全部，别担心！

sents.en: That's still a good place to start.
sents.cn: 那仍是个不错的起点。

sents.en: Start by writing down the things you didn't like about previous employers, as well as the parts you really valued.
sents.cn: 先写下你不喜欢前任雇主的地方，以及你真正看重的方面。

sents.en: There's no wrong answer here·so from big things to small details, write them all down on your list.
sents.cn: 这里没有错误答案——所以从事关重大的事到细小的细节，把它们全写进清单。

sents.en: This will help you immediately identify what you're looking for in an organization, as well as the things you're trying to stay far, far away from.
sents.cn: 这会帮你立刻弄清你在一家组织里寻找什么，以及你想远远避开的东西。

sents.en: Make sure to do your research.
sents.cn: 务必做好调查。

sents.en: Now comes the part when you put on your detective hat and do a little digging.
sents.cn: 现在到了你戴上侦探帽、稍作挖掘的时候。

sents.en: The Internet will be your best friend when you're trying to familiarize yourself with a company's culture before ever walking through their office doors.
sents.cn: 当你试图在踏入办公室门之前熟悉一家公司的文化时，互联网会是你最好的朋友。

sents.en: And where exactly should you look for these culture clues?
sents.cn: 你究竟该去哪里找这些文化线索？

sents.en: Start with the most obvious place first; the company's website.
sents.cn: 先从最显眼的地方开始：公司网站。

sents.en: Read through their copy and blog.
sents.cn: 通读他们的文案和博客。

sents.en: Do they use formal, direct language?
sents.cn: 他们用的是正式、直接的语言？

sents.en: Or is it casual, conversational, and maybe even a little humorous?
sents.cn: 还是随意、交谈式、甚至带点幽默？

sents.en: This can be a big indicator of what sort of atmosphere the company is trying to cultivate.
sents.cn: 这能强烈暗示公司想营造何种氛围。

sents.en: Next, turn your attention toward their social media outlets.
sents.cn: 接下来，把注意力转向他们的社交媒体渠道。

sents.en: Are they sharing photos of their team's Thursday afternoon barbecue or Halloween costume contest?
sents.cn: 他们是在分享团队周四下午烧烤或万圣节costume比赛的照片？

sents.en: Or are their social media accounts strictly reserved for company-related announcements and product launches?
sents.cn: 还是其社交媒体账号严格留作公司相关公告和新品发布之用？

sents.en: An industry review website like Glassdoor is another spot to check in order to find some insider information about what you can expect about a company.
sents.cn: 像Glassdoor这样的行业点评网站是另一个可查的地方，能找到关于一家公司的内部信息。

sents.en: However, remember to take the reviews you read with a grain of salt·many of them are written by scorned employees.
sents.cn: 不过，请记住对你读到的评论持保留态度——其中许多出自心怀不满的员工之手。

sents.en: Finally, you can never fail with personal connections.
sents.cn: 最后，人脉从不让你失望。在LinkedIn或邮件上给现任或前任公司员工发条简短消息，问问他们是否愿意就这家组织总体情况与你聊上几句。如果你的聊天请求得到肯定答复，走进面试时你就掌握了相当有力且有用的信息！K)Learnmorebyaskingquestions.Youknowthatpartattheendofajobinterviewwhenthehiringmanagerasksifyouhaveanyquestions,andyoujuststareacrossthetableblanklywithyourmouthhangingopen?That'stheperfectopportunitytospeakupandgetyourburningcompanyculturequestionsanswered!Soyes,youcandefinitelyaskyourintervieweraboutwhatit'sliketoworkforthatparticularorganization.Simplequestionslike,"Whatthreewordswouldyouusetodescribetheculturehere?"or"What'syourfavoritepartaboutworkingforthiscompany?"canrevealalotaboutwhatit'sreallylikebehindcloseddoors.K）通过提问了解更多。你记得工作面试结尾、招聘经理问你有没有问题时，你只是张大嘴茫然地盯着桌子对面的那一刻吧？那正是开口、把你最关心的企业文化问题弄个明白的绝佳机会！
